question.prompt: Alice, Bob, and Carol play a game in which each of them chooses a real number between \(0\) and \(1.\) The winner of the game is the one whose number is between the numbers chosen by the other two players. Alice announces that she will choose her number uniformly at random from all the numbers between \(0\) and \(1,\) and Bob announces that he will choose his number uniformly at random from all the numbers between \(\tfrac12\) and \(\tfrac23.\) Armed with this information, what number should Carol choose to maximize her chance of winning?

solutions.title: Maximize the winning probability
solutions.explanation:
Carol wins precisely when Alice and Bob choose numbers on opposite sides of hers. Let their independent choices be \(X\) and \(Y\), and let Carol choose \(c\). Ties have probability zero.

First consider choices outside Bob's interval. If \(0\le c\le\tfrac12\), Bob's number is above \(c\), so Carol wins exactly when \(X<c\). Her winning probability is \(c\), at most \(\tfrac12\). If \(\tfrac23\le c\le1\), Bob's number is below \(c\), so her winning probability is \(1-c\), at most \(\tfrac13\).

It remains to consider \(\tfrac12<c<\tfrac23\). Uniformity means that Bob's probabilities are the appropriate interval-length ratios:
\[
P(Y>c)=\frac{\frac23-c}{\frac23-\frac12}=4-6c,
\qquad
P(Y<c)=6c-3.
\]
For Alice, \(P(X<c)=c\) and \(P(X>c)=1-c\). Independence lets us multiply probabilities within each winning case. Since the cases \(X<c<Y\) and \(Y<c<X\) are disjoint, we add their probabilities:
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(\text{Carol wins})
&=c(4-6c)+(1-c)(6c-3)\\
&=-12c^2+13c-3.
\end{aligned}
\]
This quadratic opens downward, so its maximum occurs at its vertex,
\[
c=-\frac{13}{2(-12)}=\frac{13}{24}.
\]
This is in Bob's interval because \(\tfrac12=\tfrac{12}{24}<\tfrac{13}{24}<\tfrac{16}{24}=\tfrac23\). The resulting winning probability is
\[
-12\left(\frac{13}{24}\right)^2
+13\left(\frac{13}{24}\right)-3
=\frac{-169+338-144}{48}
=\frac{25}{48}.
\]
Since \(\tfrac{25}{48}>\tfrac12>\tfrac13\), this beats the best probabilities in both outside cases. Carol should choose \(\boxed{\tfrac{13}{24}}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
